title: Luna affine attraction neighbourhoods stable under the common unipotent subgroup
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field]. All algebraic groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Solvable groups, unipotent groups and tori have the meanings of [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]: solvability is termination of successive commutator subgroup schemes, a smooth group is unipotent when its geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation, and a torus is isomorphic to $(\mathbf G_m)^r$ for some $r\geq0$. A Borel subgroup of a smooth connected group is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup; a maximal torus is a torus subgroup maximal under inclusion. Let $G$ be smooth and connected, let $T\subseteq G$ be a maximal torus, and let $X=\mathcal B(G)$ and $b_B\in X(k)$ denote the flag variety and its Borel-labelled points of [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety]. Let $V\subseteq G$ be any smooth connected unipotent subgroup such that $V\subseteq B'$ for every Borel subgroup $B'\supseteq T$. For every Borel $B\supseteq T$, there is an affine open subscheme $A_B\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose rational points are $$A_B(k)=\{b_{B'}\in X(k):b_B\in\overline{T(k)\cdot b_{B'}}\}.$$ The bar denotes closure in the underlying Zariski topological space of $X$. The action of $V$ on $X$ restricts to $V\times_k A_B\to A_B$, and the closed complement $|X|\setminus|A_B|$ is invariant under $V(k)$. No assertion that $V$ is normal in $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 17.65 and its proof, printed p.374; its proof only uses containment of the unipotent acting subgroup in every Borel containing T to obtain containment in the parabolic stabilizer of the dual line. Thus it applies to every V as stated, before any conclusion of Theorem 17.56.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety], $X$ is smooth connected projective, its $k$-points form one $G(k)$-orbit, and the scheme stabilizer of $b_B$ is $B$. Thus [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] identifies $X$ equivariantly with $G/B$. Apply [lem-sfb-general-flag-isolated-linear-action] to obtain a $G$-equivariant closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ and a cocharacter $\mu$ with $X^\mu$ finite reduced and nonempty. Use [lem-sfb-cocharacter-conjugate-maximal-torus] to conjugate $\mu$ into the prescribed $T$. Conjugation acts on $X$ by an automorphism, so the new fixed subscheme remains finite reduced. The closed subscheme $X^T$ is contained in this finite reduced fixed subscheme, hence is itself finite reduced; it is nonempty because $b_B$ is fixed by $T$.

source.place: Theorem 17.65, first paragraph; Theorems 4.27, 17.10 and Section 17f.

proof.text: Replace $E$ by the vector subspace $E_0$ spanned by the lines $i(x)$ for $x\in X(k)$. It is $G(k)$-stable, hence a rational $G$-subrepresentation by [lem-sfb-smooth-group-rational-point-subspace-test]. Since $X$ is smooth over $k$, [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] makes it reduced. Each linear equation of $\mathbf P(E_0)$ vanishes on $i(X(k))$; on affine charts its pullback is zero by the vanishing principle of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing]. Hence $i$ factors as a closed immersion into $\mathbf P(E_0)$. Rename $E_0$ as $E$. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-torus-extreme-weight-affine-chart] now hold. Obtain separating $\lambda$, minimum weight line $k e_0=i(x_0)$, functional $f_0$, and affine chart $U=i^{-1}D(f_0)$ with its stated torus-orbit-closure description.

source.place: Theorem 17.65, nondegenerate embedding and weight paragraphs; Propositions 13.52--13.53.

proof.text: The point $x_0$ is $T$-fixed, so [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety] writes it as $b_{B_0}$ with $T\subseteq B_0$. By [lem-sfb-torus-normalizer-borel-transitivity], choose $n\in G(k)$ normalizing $T$ with $nB_0n^{-1}=B$. Conjugate the weight decomposition and $\lambda$ by $n$, and replace $e_0,f_0,U$ by $\rho(n)e_0,\rho^\vee(n)f_0,nU$, where $\rho^\vee(g)f=f\circ\rho(g)^{-1}$. These still have the minimum-weight coordinate description. Because $nTn^{-1}=T$, conjugation carries $x_0\in\overline{T(k)y}$ exactly to $b_B\in\overline{T(k)(ny)}$. Thus after renaming, $x_0=b_B$ and $U$ has exactly the rational points required of $A_B$.

source.place: Theorem 17.65, normalizer translation of the attracting point; Proposition 17.53.

proof.text: Let $O=G\cdot[f_0]\subseteq\mathbf P(E^*)$ for the contragredient representation. By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry], this is a smooth locally closed orbit, with invariant closed boundary $Z=\overline O\setminus O$. Put $D=\{[f]:f(e_0)\ne0\}$. Every $G(k)$-orbit in $\mathbf P(E^*)(k)$ meets $D$: otherwise a nonzero representative $f$ annihilates all $\rho(g)e_0$, which span $E$ since $G(k)x_0=X(k)$. On $D$, normalize $f(e_0)=1$. Under $\lambda(t)^{-1}$ each remaining dual coordinate is multiplied by $t^{m_\chi-m_{\chi_0}}$, a strictly positive power; hence its limit at zero is $[f_0]$. If $Z$ were nonempty it would contain a $k$-point, by [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] on a nonempty affine chart. Move that point into $D$. Invariance and closedness of $Z$ put its limit $[f_0]$ in $Z$, a contradiction. Consequently $Z$ is empty, so $O$ is closed in projective space and is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper].

source.place: Theorem 17.65, dual-representation paragraph; orbit boundary as in Sections 1 and 7.

proof.text: The dual line $[f_0]$ is fixed scheme-theoretically by $T$, because $f_0$ is a character eigenvector. The orbit $O$ is nonempty smooth connected proper and $G(k)$-transitive. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-homogeneous-torus-borel-stabilizer] to obtain a Borel $C$ with $T\subseteq C$ fixing this dual line on every algebra. The assumption on $V$ gives $V\subseteq C$. Thus $V$ preserves the direct-summand line $k f_0$ in $E^*$. On a commutative $k$-algebra $A$, every $v\in V(A)$ acts on $A f_0$ by a unit $c(v)\in A^\times$, so $f_0(\rho_A(v)e)=c(v)^{-1}f_0(e)$ for $e\in E\otimes_k A$. Therefore $\rho(v)$ preserves the open condition $f_0\ne0$ and its hyperplane complement. Equivariance of $i$ gives the restricted action $V\times_k U\to U$. For each $v\in V(k)$ the automorphism and its inverse preserve the complement, so $|X|\setminus|U|$ is $V(k)$-invariant. Taking $A_B=U$ proves all clauses.

source.place: Theorem 17.65, final sentences: containment in a Borel through T fixes the dual line, hence the open cell.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 17.65 and proof, printed p.374; the argument is applied to any subgroup contained in every Borel through T, using only that containment.

tool_uses.why: Smoothness over the field makes X reduced, needed to restrict the embedding to the span of its rational points.
The reduced finite-type vanishing principle identifies the projective span scheme-theoretically; its closed-point clause also detects a nonempty dual-orbit boundary.
A closed projective dual orbit is proper, allowing the Borel stabilizer theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q39-addc43eba (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full the item's 5 steps, the 3 new unsplit statement nodes, every cited statement, and Milne iAG2017 Theorem 17.65 with its proof (printed p.374). The item statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live, and the item is still unsplit in live and side-live. The steps follow Milne's route: (1) general-borel-flag-variety, homogeneous-orbit-quotient, the isolated linear action, and the new cocharacter conjugacy moving the cocharacter into the prescribed T; X^T is a union of components of the finite reduced fixed scheme, and b_B makes it nonempty. (2) Restrict to the span of the points via the rational-point subspace test, reducedness and the Nullstellensatz vanishing clause; the hypotheses of the extreme chart node then hold. (3) Normalizer transitivity; checked y∈nU ⇔ b_B ∈ closure(T·y). (4) Every dual orbit meets D(e0), λ^{-1} contracts it to [f0], a nonempty boundary has a k-point, so the dual orbit is closed and proper. (5) The new stabilizer node gives a Borel C ⊇ T fixing [f0]; V ⊆ C, ρ^∨(v)f0 = c·f0 makes D(f0) V-stable on A-points. New nodes: cocharacter conjugacy is true (Milne 17.10) and no DAG node states torus conjugacy. The extreme-weight chart I proved independently: the projection of the dense open to the finite set P(E_χ0)∩X is constant, so E_χ0 is a line; both inclusions of U(k) hold; tested on P1, r=0 and trivial actions. The proper-homogeneous stabilizer is true: Borel fixed point, transitivity, then conjugating T inside ((G_y)_red)^0; tested on a point, SL2 on P1 and non-smooth stabilizers. None restates the item or duplicates projective-attracting-cells, flag-torus-fixed-geometry or solvable-proper-fixed-point. Refs, stmt_deps and the union of proof_deps were checked mechanically; no SGA. The tool_uses (smooth⇒reduced, Nullstellensatz, projective⇒proper) are generic and accepted. Batch-5 flag: homogeneous-orbit-quotient reaches lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change, a generic Mathlib leaf on fppf base change that is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so it is not a RETURN. Minor unwritten elementary details in step 5 (the action restricts to the reduced orbit; G(k) is transitive on O(k)) were accepted. No fixes.
